points.description: Structure: a bipartite graph / two layers (visible and hidden) of binary neurons, connected recurrently (no connections within a layer).
points.partial_credit: Half if only layers named or only 'bipartite' without visible/hidden.

points.description: Core mechanism: neurons' binary states are flipped/set stochastically, with a probability determined by the neuron's activation.
points.partial_credit: Half if stochastic/binary mentioned but link to activation-based probability is missing or vague.

points.description: Two phases/states: clamped state (visible neurons connected to/fixed by the input) and free-running state (both layers run freely).
points.partial_credit: Half if only one of the two states is correctly described.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the bipartite visible/hidden structure, stochastic binary neuron updates driven by activation probability, and the clamped vs free-running states. Give part marks for ideas stated vaguely or with only one half present. Give no marks for descriptions of other networks (e.g. feed-forward or Hopfield only) with none of these ideas. Different wording is fine.
